description:
FOUND s499k (Opus, 2026-09-27) probing #2443.  PRE-EXISTING (identical on main 937e7b65).

Reproducer (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL):
    my $r2 = qr/a b/; print "ab" =~ /x|$r2/x ? 1 : 0, "\n";      # perl 0   PCL 1
    my $p = '(?^:^a ++b)'; print eval { "a  b" =~ /$p/x ? 1 : 0 } // "died", "\n";   # perl 1   PCL died

CAUSE: perl-regex-to-ppcre turns `(?^FLAGS:` into `(?FLAGS:` ("at the top level the semantics are identical"), but `^` RESETS every flag to the default first, so a qr// interpolated into a bigger /x pattern keeps /x OFF inside its own group.  With the `^` gone cl-ppcre applies the outer /x inside the group: `a b` loses its blank (silent wrong: matches "ab"), and `a ++` loses the blank the possessive applies to (dies).  The same holds for /i /m /s in principle (`qr/a/` inside `/x$r/i`), though the lone-qr spelling `/$re/i` is right because the object is used as is (#181).

FIX SHAPE (not tried): translate `(?^FLAGS:` to `(?FLAGS-<imsx not in FLAGS>:` — cl-ppcre supports inline negated flags, and a `-x` makes %pcl-has-x-modifier route the pattern through %pcl-normalize-extended, which already honours the caret (%pcl-parse-x-flag-group).  Since s499k the rewrite scan runs BEFORE the `(?^` removal and already reads the caret for its own /x tracking, so the scan is not the blocker.  Probe /i /m /s /x and the qr stringification round trip; ir-spec §10 compiled-regex row.
subject: SILENT WRONG (pre-existing): a qr// interpolated into a /x pattern takes the OUTER /x inside its (?^:...) group -- the caret reset is dropped (qr/a b/ in /x|$r/x matches "ab")
